subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance benchmarks, latency/cost targets, and steward ownership
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.h@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Velez <alicia.velez@novasight.ai>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@novasight.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed acceptance benchmarks and ops steward

Hi Alicia / Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed, lean acceptance benchmark set we can use to confirm success during the 4-week evaluation. I kept it tight so your engineering team can start instrumentation now.

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Main objective: Replace current in-house summarization microservice for customer-facing digests; critical constraints are strict 1s p95 latency on short requests and predictable cost per 1k tokens.
- Typical production workload: 60 qps bursty (peak 120 qps), median request length 120 tokens, predictable distribution of short (<=64) vs long (200-600) sequences.
- Success priority: 1) latency for short/light requests, 2) cost/token reduction vs baseline, 3) fidelity on extractive summaries (ROUGE-L and manual spot checks).

Proposed acceptance benchmarks (minimal viable acceptance):
- Latency: p95 <= 1.0s for requests <= 128 tokens under steady-state throughput of 60 qps on your sampled workload.
- Throughput: system sustains 60 qps steady and handles 120 qps 60-second bursts with <15% increase in p95 latency vs steady-state.
- Cost: average effective cost <= $0.020 per 1k tokens (token accounting as per our SDK instrumentation) — two-week rolling average during test window.
- Quality: automated ROUGE-L >= 0.48 against your golden set (n=120) AND no more than 6% regression in manual qualitative score across 20 spot-checks vs your baseline.
- Operational: no unhandled 5xx errors; error rate <= 0.2% of requests.

Ownership and run cadence:
- Eval owner (Redwood): Ben Carter — will coordinate infra, runbook, and cost telemetry.
- Eval owner (Novasight): Alicia — will provide golden set, workload traces, and a sandbox credential.
- Weekly syncs: Tuesdays 10:00am PT; ramp plan and checkpoints attached.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Alicia: share 7-day sample traces + golden set by Wed 07/07 (attachment: sample-workload.jsonl).
2) Ben: provision dedicated sandbox and share endpoint + token by Fri 07/09.
3) Mina: deliver evaluation matrix + measurement workbook by Mon 07/12 (attachment: novasight-eval-metrics-template.xlsx).

If this looks reasonable, we can lock the timeline and I’ll open the HubSpot milestone and invite your infra lead to the first sync.

Thanks — happy to tighten any of these if your team has stronger guardrails.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference — production-first inference for LLMs

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed acceptance benchmarks and ops steward

Thanks Mina — this is super clear and valuable. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token accounting: we report tokens slightly differently (we include prompt + context). We'll provide the exact counting script. Can you confirm Redwood's SDK will align or we should normalize after collection?
2) Quality: the golden set currently has 150 items; we can carve 120 as you suggested but want to keep the extra 30 for stress testing.
3) Timeline: 07/07 for traces is fine; we may need your help to redact PII from traces — can Ben advise if Redwood will do that or if you need them sanitized before upload?

Also, one ask from our infra: can you provide an explicit fallback plan if the p95 latency target is missed during burst testing (e.g., auto-fallback to smaller model with acceptable quality degradation)? Samir is including our infra specialist on the thread in case we need deeper ops coordination.

Alicia
Director of Product Ops | Novasight AI
alicia.velez@novasight.ai | +1 (212) 555-0199

Hi Alicia / Samir — adding a few operational notes and answers to Mina/Alicia's questions: 

- Token accounting: Redwood's SDK emits both model-token usage and a "normalized_token_count" that mirrors prompt+context counting. We'll surface both in the workbook so you can map to your billing metrics.
- Redaction: If you cannot remove PII upstream, we can accept traces in the provided sandbox bucket and run our redaction pipeline (redaction adds a day to the onboarding timeline). Recommend you try to sanitize first — but we'll handle if needed.
- Fallback / graceful degradation: We will configure a policy in the sandbox that falls back to a smaller, quantized model variant when p95 exceeds 1.2s for two consecutive minutes. Expect a quality delta — we'll capture that in the evaluation matrix.

I've attached a short runbook (first tab in the workbook) and included the proposed canary/fallback thresholds.

Operational owners:
- Redwood infra lead (sandbox): Ben Carter (me) — endpoint, tokens, redaction pipeline.
- Redwood exec sponsor: Mina Haddad — product & acceptance.
- Novasight infra: Samir (ops) and Alicia (product ops).

I’ll provision the sandbox today and email credentials. Mina — I left a few measurement rows for ROUGE variants; feel free to tweak.

Ben
Senior Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | +1 (650) 555-0098

- Also toggling the weekly sync to 10:30am PT works better for our ops lead — see updated invite.

Alicia / Ben — appreciate the rapid turnaround. Looking forward to the first smoke validation.
